heading: EXT. COLLAPSED SALT CAVE - SAHARA FRINGE - DAY

units.text: EXT. COLLAPSED SALT CAVE - SAHARA FRINGE - DAY
A mouth of white rock half buried in drift.
Heat shimmers.
Three survivors huddle in a shallow slice of shade.

KOFI AMOAH-LINDQVIST (40s, torn flight jacket) kneels by a puddle of brackish water and filters it through his shirt, while TAMSIN PARRY-OYELARAN (30s, bandaged forearm) leans against the stone and presses a swollen tongue against cracked lips, and young EZEQUIEL "ZEKE" MARTINEAU (teens, plastic-framed glasses held on with tape) draws a line in the sand with a stick, over and over, as if it might become a road.
Three cups. Maybe four.
units.name: KOFI

units.text: Tamsin nods.
Zeke keeps drawing.
That's a day. Maybe two if we're careful.
units.name: KOFI

units.text: Zeke draws another line, crossing the first.
Kofi hands Tamsin the cup.
She holds it a long moment, then passes it to Zeke without drinking.
Zeke looks at the cup, then at her, then at the line he has drawn.
He sips once.
He hands the cup back to Kofi.
Kofi, without a word, lifts it to his lips, swallows, and puts it down on the stone between them.
A shadow crosses the sand.
All three look up.
A bird, high and slow, wheels over the white ridge.
Tamsin shields her eyes.
Kofi rises to a crouch.
Zeke drops the stick.
The bird circles, tilts, and drops out of sight beyond the rocks.
For a long moment nobody moves.
Then Kofi picks up the stick, steps over Zeke's lines, and begins to walk.
